senses.gloss: (b. h. שָׂרַט; contr. of סחרט, Saf. of חָרַט) to make an incision; to mark.
units: <cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 11:6">Tosef. Sabb. XI</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 12:6">XII</cite>), 6 <he>הסוֹרֵט סריטה וכ׳</he> he who draws one mark over two boards at the same time; (<cite ref="Shabbat 103b:2">Sabb. 103ᵇ</cite> <he>שָׂרַט שריטה</he>).
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 33">Gen. R. s. 33</cite>, end <he>יִסְרוֹט לו סריטה וכ׳</he> let him make a mark on the wall (indicating the standing of the sun) &c.

Ex. R. s. 12, beg. ס׳ לו סריטה וכ׳ (Tanḥ. Vaëra 16 ש׳ לו שריטה) he drew a mark for him on the wall &c. Lam. R. introd. (Zabdi 2); ib. to IV, 12 (ref. to Is. X, 19) ששה שכן … להיות שׂורֵט שריטה six were left over, for that is a child’s way to make a stroke (resembling ו = six); (Midr. Till. to Ps. LXXIX, beg.; v. ed. Bub. note 21) ; a. fr.—Esp. to wound the body in mourning, v. שָׂרַט.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 12:4">Sabb. XII, 4</cite> <he>המְסָרֵט על בשרו</he> he who makes a mark on his body by scratching, contrad. to <he>הכותב</he>.

<cite ref="Sotah 48a:8">Sot. 48ᵃ</cite> (expl. <he>נוקפין</he>) <he>שהיו מְסָרְטִין לעגל וכ׳</he> they used to make a scratch between the calf’s horns, that the blood might run over its eyes; (<cite ref="Tosefta Sotah 13:10">Tosef. Sot. XIII, 10</cite> <he>שמכין</he>, ed. Zuck. <he>שמושכין</he>).

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 24">Ex. R. s. 24</cite> <he>שאילולי היה … ומְשָׂרֶטֶת אותו</he> if a man were to eat (and swallow) a piece of bread in its natural condition (not softened by the moisture of saliva), it would enter his entrails and wound him; a. e.—[<cite ref="Tosefta Bava Metzia 3:29">Tosef. B. Mets. III, 29</cite> <he>משרבטין ומסרטין</he>, strike out <he>ומסרטין</he> as a corrupt dittography of <he>משרבטין</he>; v. ed. Zuck.]—V. <cite ref="U01951"><he>שָׂרַט</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Shabbat 53b:16">Sabb. 53ᵇ</cite> <he>כדי שלא יִסָּרְטוּ דדיהן</he> that their udders may not be scratched (when passing between bushes).
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 2:5">Ex. R. s. 2</cite> <he>וכשהוא מוציאה מִסְתָּרֶטֶת</he> but when he takes his hand out, it will be wounded.
